key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary between Sn fractions x = 0.60 and 0.65 in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn mixing offers a route to tune structural order and band gaps in lead-free perovskites, with potential relevance to solar-cell absorber design.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map temperature-dependent structural phases and band-gap trends.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce both end members’ known transition sequences and temperatures, reveal an intermediate I4/mcm phase, and predict a low-temperature band-gap jump that becomes a smooth composition trend at 350 K.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational phase and band-gap predictions, not experimental validation of alloy behavior or solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
